name: Friedrich Wilhelm I of Prussia
role: King in Prussia and Elector of Brandenburg (1713–1740)
summary: Frederick William I centralized royal administration and expanded Prussia’s standing army. His rule combined protectionist economic development and Protestant piety with selective religious toleration and coercive social discipline.

sources.title: Political Testament (February 17, 1722)
sources.author: Frederick William I; translated by C. A. Macartney
sources.usedFor: Dynasty, sovereign authority, religious and cultural regulation, selective toleration, foreign policy and relief.

sources.title: Instructions on the Formation and Functioning of the General Directory (December 20, 1722)
sources.author: Frederick William I; translated by C. A. Macartney
sources.usedFor: Tariffs, manufacturing, capital controls, taxation, serf obligations and punishment.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His instructions favor official direction of industry and capital over unrestricted market allocation.

empower-police-military.rationale: He personally doubled the army and increased its officer corps.

decide-locally.rationale: He rejects provincial privileges that constrain royal sovereignty.

more-religion-public.rationale: He makes Christian piety a governing duty.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He invited displaced Salzburg Protestants to repopulate East Prussia; this was selective immigration.

free-trade.rationale: He prohibited foreign manufactured imports and exports of domestic raw materials to foster Prussian industry.

nation-first.rationale: Alliances must serve Prussian interests, rather than foreign subsidies.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Article X orders heavy import duties to undercut foreign manufactures.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Article XII directs officials to introduce manufacturing, following his Potsdam musket factory.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His 1739 edict opposed landlords’ expropriation of peasant holdings, though he retained substantial crown estates.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He instructs his royal successor to preserve the dynasty.

democracy-best.rationale: Inferred: his defense of unlimited royal sovereignty as a divine duty conflicts with popular supremacy.

collective-farming.rationale: His 1718 rebuilding plan allocates separate farms and livestock to individual peasant households.

taxation-theft.rationale: He requires full, punctual collection of war taxes and universal payment of excise, including by his household.

conscription.rationale: He established the canton system and expanded peasants’ military obligations.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He demands land and population as rewards for military cooperation.

bound-labor.rationale: Article VII preserves landlords’ dues while prohibiting unbearable burdens on unfree peasants.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: He seeks higher revenues from the Wettin coal mines.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: His 1718 settlement instructions establish village schoolmasters to guide peasants toward God.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred: his account of sovereignty as divinely ordained royal duty does not make legitimacy conditional on subjects’ consent.

population-transfer.rationale: He demands expulsion of Jews without royal protection letters.

separated-powers.rationale: Inferred: exclusive royal control of army and finances rules out independent checks.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He reserves army command and financial control personally to the monarch.

clerical-rule.rationale: He expressly excludes preachers from directing secular affairs.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He demands bans on opera, ballet and comedy as sinful.

people-in-arms.rationale: He enlarged and intensively drilled the standing army rather than replacing it with citizen militias.

death-penalty.rationale: Article XIV prescribes hanging for convicted helpers of military deserters.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He restrained clergy’s political agitation and used royal authority to supervise ecclesiastical affairs.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The biography describes his claim to unlimited royal authority as both a right and a duty.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: his son’s planned succession endorses inheritance over election.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: his assertion of unlimited royal authority places the monarch above any parliamentary claim to supreme lawmaking.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred: exclusive royal financial control precludes parliamentary budget approval.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He accuses Jesuits of plotting against ruler and community.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The biography records his justification of sovereign royal authority through divine ordinance.

dynastic-succession.rationale: His testament explicitly prepares his son to inherit rule.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He orders publicly supported village schooling expressly intended to cultivate religious belief.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He forbids aggression, while bargaining for territory through military alliances.

capital-controls.rationale: Article X requires preventing residents from transferring capital abroad.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: His testament prescribes permanent hard labor for repeat wool-import offenders.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: He equalizes Lutherans and Calvinists, but excludes Jesuits.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He would remove refugee pensions from recipients already well-off.

notes: The 1722 testament and administrative instructions are read alongside evidence from the remainder of his reign. His later recommendation of Wolff’s philosophy prevents treating the 1723 expulsion as his final position on philosophical study. Selective Protestant immigration does not establish support for open borders; limited Christian toleration does not establish universal religious equality. Modern issues without matching evidence remain null.
